Tremulous

/TREM-yuh-luhs/ - the stress falls on TREM · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tremulous means shaking slightly from emotion or nervousness.

He signed the loan papers with a tremulous flourish, equal parts excitement and terror.

Worked Example

On the first morning of her bakery's reopening, Lena's hands were tremulous as she cut the ribbon—not fear, the reporters decided, but eleven months of hope arriving all at once.

Tremulous names a slight, visible shaking with feeling or nerves behind it—smaller than 'shaking,' more human than 'unsteady.' A voice, a hand, a smile can each be tremulous; an earthquake never is.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

quivering: shaking in small rapid movements; tremulous adds the emotional cause

shaky: the plain word for unsteady movement of any kind

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

steady: holding without a waver

firm: fixed and unshaking, in grip or voice

Where it sits · how violently the shaking spreads — wobbly → tremulous → convulsive

wobbly vs. tremulous: Wobbly stops short of tremulous — wobbly is a matter of balance, while tremulous is a fine visible shiver of feeling.

convulsive vs. tremulous: Convulsive goes further than tremulous — a convulsive shudder shakes the whole body, not just the voice or the hands.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — trem-

Root — trem-: to shake (Latin tremere)

Suffix — -ulous

Suffix — -ulous: tending to

Put it together

Put it together: Trem- (to shake) + -ulous (tending to) = tending to shake. Latin tremere, 'to tremble,' also gives English tremor and tremble itself — the same shiver at three sizes. Tremulous is the fine, human-scale one: the shake of a voice or a hand under feeling.

Use the root in a new word: tremor

Use the root in a new word: tremor: A slight tremor rattled the teacups but spared every shelf.

Word Choice

literary

Tremulous is the writer's word for a small, telling shake — a voice, a signature, a candle-lit smile. Plain 'shaky' does the everyday work. Its unit-mate timorous is the temperament behind the shake: timorous is being easily frightened; tremulous is what the fright looks like.
